description: Compare native window and content corners across page borders, split layouts, sidebar states and fullscreen.
preconditions: Launch the exact newly built Dev bundle on the isolated profile and record the macOS version.
Use a plain page with a bright solid background so its clip is visible against the window frame.
steps: At browser UI scales 100%, 110% and 125%, compare frame borders 0, 6 and 24 points with the sidebar expanded, collapsed and fully hidden.
Hide and reveal the top bar, then inspect all four page corners while resizing and zooming the window.
Create a side-by-side split, then a stacked split. Change the frame border and inspect both outer corners and the divider corners.
Enter fullscreen with a single page and each split orientation, then exit fullscreen. Repeat with the sidebar hidden.
Move the window between displays with different backing scales when available.
On macOS 27, repeat with the user's existing customized window policy when present; do not change global defaults for the test.
Quit normally and relaunch the same profile, then close its windows and stop the isolated app.
observables: Window-facing content corners follow the actual native window curve after accounting for their adjacent frame insets. A border wider than that curve produces a square corner without a negative radius.
Single pages and split outer corners use the same configured frame width. Internal split corners retain the generic rounded style.
A stacked split gives both top window corners to the top pane and both bottom window corners to the bottom pane.
Sidebar and top-bar changes retain generic interior corners next to attached chrome. No extra native mask clips page content twice.
Fullscreen has no inherited window-corner cutout, and exiting fullscreen restores the current native policy without restarting.
Resizing, zooming, browser scale and display changes leave no stale corner geometry or clipped input targets.
Saved frame settings survive normal relaunch; closing and quitting produce no new crash report.
